title: Automated Creator Outreach: How to Scale Creator Messages Without Sounding Like a Bot
summary: Learn how automated creator outreach works end to end: AI creator search, personalized sequences across DM, Target Collab and email, reply handling, and GMV tracking.
body_markdown:
## The End-to-End Outreach Workflow, Step by Step


Automate organization and repetition, then make human review visible wherever a creator’s experience or your brand’s commitments are at stake. Reacher’s[AI Creator Search](https://www.reacherapp.com/features/creator-discovery) ranks a database of more than 4 million TikTok Shop creators. Reacher outreach runs across DM, Target Collab, and email at up to 10,000 creators a day. That is platform capacity, not a recommended quota. Set your pace according to channel rules, account health, and your team’s ability to handle replies.


### Step 1: AI Creator Search From a Plain-English Description (Profile, Transcript, Visual, Lookalike)


Start with the creator you need, not a broad follower-count filter. Describe the audience, content style, category, and product fit in plain English, then refine the shortlist against campaign requirements. Search four ways: use a plain-English profile description, a creator transcript, a product image, or a lookalike of a creator already working with you. Profile search starts from a written description; transcript search looks at what creators say; visual search uses a product image or prompt; and lookalike search uses a creator handle or CRM group.


### Step 2: Build a Multi-Channel Sequence Across DM, Target Collab, and Email


Choose the first channel according to the creator’s available contact route and campaign workflow. Use DM, Target Collab, and email as coordinated options, not simultaneous copies of the same pitch. If there is no response, use an appropriate alternate channel only when permitted. Keep one contact history so teammates do not duplicate messages or overlook replies.


### Step 3: Draft a Unique Message Per Creator With Preview Before Send


Give each draft a clear structure: creator name, a specific content reference, product fit, key selling point, offer details, and one next step. Reacher’s personalized outreach drafts a unique message using creator and campaign context, with tone control and an exact-message preview before sending. Review claims about product benefits, compensation, and campaign expectations. Correct errors before approval instead of relying on a template to interpret them.


### Step 4: Handle Replies With AI Chatbot Triage and Human Handoff


Use automated handling for routine questions with approved answers, such as where to find campaign details. Route negotiations, product concerns, unusual requests, and unclear intent to a person. Assign an owner, preserve the conversation, and pause follow-ups while the reply is under review. This organizes response handling without letting a chatbot make promises or miss relationship cues.


### Step 5: Route Samples Through One Queue With Weekly Caps


Review sample requests in one queue. Check creator fit, inventory, campaign rules, and shipping details before approval. Weekly caps help teams manage fulfillment capacity and avoid approving more requests than they can process. Record each decision and sample status so creators receive clear updates and the team can see which requests are pending, approved, or declined.


### Step 6: Track Status, Messages, and GMV Per Creator in One CRM


Record outreach status, message history, sample activity, content progress, and GMV per creator. A shared CRM distinguishes a new prospect from a contacted creator, active affiliate, or partner who needs follow-up. Reacher’s[creator CRM](https://www.reacherapp.com/features/creator-crm) connects status, messages, samples, and GMV in one system. Use these records to assess which recruitment sources and creator profiles merit attention, rather than judging success by sent-message counts alone.
